title: challenge-fires-at-intent
intention: Give /challenge a FIRING EVENT. It becomes a required step inside /intent — the moment a node is born — rather than an optional route mentioned in passing and a cadence scheduled against a clock that does not exist.
why: MEASURED 2026-07-26. Akien: 'i haven't been using challenge. is it called in our skills?' It is referenced in exactly three places and fired by none: intent/SKILL.md:56 says 'IF the design wants an adversarial pass' (optional); intent/intention+why.json:15 lists it as '(optional adversarial pass)'; sorted/SKILL.md:22 fires the challenge GATE, which the challenge charter itself calls a DIFFERENT PLACEMENT of the same pose, not the skill. CLAUDE.md:97 schedules it 'on a cadence' — a cadence with no trigger never fires. So the skill whose five questions include 'PRIOR ART?' has never once asked it. In one session that cost three stumbles onto already-solved work (an hour re-deriving a storage design that was on disk with tests; 'no inference host' with ollama serving four days; nearly rebuilding the bus VERB that UU had solved as a declared-capability Channel). The question existed. Nothing asked it.
traces_to: Law 1 — the resolver spent re-deriving the settled is a defect; 'prior art?' is the question that stops it, and it must fire before the build, not after.
Law 4 — a rule that matters is enforced by physics, not policy. 'Remember to run /challenge' is policy. A required step inside /intent is closer to physics.
memory shrinking-footprint-event-not-poll — the fix is the EVENT that already fires (a node being born), never a clock. A cadence was the poll, and it polled zero times.

proves_green.prove_gate: the skill class's proof gate, plus the cairnmap recompile gate a skill node hangs.

falsifier.proves_red: /intent's step list must carry /challenge as a REQUIRED step, not a route or a suggestion — and the skill's proof must assert that, so a future edit softening it back to optional goes RED. Second clause: the prior-art question must have somewhere to look. Once quarry-index is built, a /challenge run on a node whose idea exists in the quarry must SURFACE it; a run that consults nothing and returns 'no prior art' is the hollow build this falsifier exists to catch.
falsifier.horizon: Re-read after the first three /intent runs under the change. If the challenge step is being satisfied with a token 'considered, none found', the step is present but hollow and this reopens as a question-quality problem rather than a wiring one.
